title: Matryoshka
summary: A matryoshka is a hollow wooden doll, turned from lime or birch, that opens to show a smaller doll inside and so on down to a solid one no bigger than a bean. Its round, flared body is painted as a woman in a kerchief, apron and flowered skirt.
howToPlay: Look at the doll in the frame: a narrow foot, wide hips, a rounded head.
Drag across each row of the spinning wood to set how wide it is.
Press Glaze, choose a colour and fill the five bands from skirt to kerchief.
Press Check to see how close your doll is.
rules: Twelve rows of wood, each from one to ten steps wide.
Seventy points for the outline and thirty for the colour bands.
Three stars need an almost exact shape and colours in the right order.
heritageNote: The first Russian set was turned in a Moscow workshop in the 1890s, and makers in Sergiyev Posad, Semyonov and Polkhovsky Maidan later developed their own faces, scarves and flowers. Dolls are turned on a lathe from seasoned linden, each shell made to fit the next, then painted by hand and varnished.
